headline: Apple refreshes iMac with M6 chips, skipping M5 entirely for a major performance boost
summary: The all-in-one desktop now features Apple's first 2nm M6 chip, boosting performance for on-device AI tasks and starting at $1,499.
details: Apple has updated its iMac line with the new M6 chips, giving the all-in-one desktop a significant performance boost. Prices for the refreshed iMac start from $1,499, with the design remaining largely unchanged from its predecessor.

This update comes two years after the M4 iMac overhaul, meaning the M5 series is skipped for this hardware. The M6 is Apple's first 2nm chip, incorporating a dual 16-core Neural Engine designed to enhance on-device AI task performance.
Compared to the M4 iMac's 8-core CPU, the M6 configurations start with a 10-core CPU and a 10-core GPU. This upgrade aims to provide a more meaningful performance leap for users.

headline: Opera One lets users run AI models locally in the browser via WebAI, starting today
summary: Opera One introduces a preview feature allowing users to deploy AI models directly within the browser, leveraging a new proposed web standard called WebAI.
details: Starting today, Opera One users can access a preview feature that enables them to tap into local AI models directly within the browser. This functionality is powered by WebAI, a newly proposed web standard.

The WebAI standard aims to allow web browsers to interact with local AI models, bringing AI processing closer to the user's device. This could offer benefits in terms of privacy, speed, and offline capabilities.

By running AI models locally, users can process data without sending it to cloud servers, enhancing data privacy. It also reduces latency, as computations are performed directly on the user's machine.
This move by Opera positions it at the forefront of integrating local AI capabilities into web browsing. It signifies a potential shift towards more decentralized AI applications on the web.

The initial implementation in Opera One allows users to experiment with various AI models. This includes completion models for writing and conversation, and embedding models for search and recall functions.
